hint.text: Some objects may look like verbs at first. Take a careful look.

instruction.text: The object you selected above is also known as a gerund. Look at the sentence again and fill in the gap.

atoms.b: Gerunds are a type of ((++noun verb adverb)) made from the -ing form of a verb. Gerunds and gerund phrases can act as subjects or objects of verbs.
atoms.sound: Gerunds are a type of noun made from the i n g form of a verb. Gerunds and gerund phrases can act as subjects or objects of verbs.

instruction.text: Rewrite each of the verbs below as a gerund to complete the sentence.

atoms.b: 1. Her ((singing)) has improved ever since she joined a choir.
atoms.sound: Her singing has improved ever since she joined a choir.

atoms.b: 2. He recalls ((seeing)) an old record you were looking for.
atoms.sound: He recalls seeing an old record you were looking for.

atoms.b: 3. Although he knows it’s partially irrational, he is still anxious about ((flying)).
atoms.sound: Although he knows it’s partially irrational, he is still anxious about flying.

atoms.b: 4. ((Thinking)) for too long often complicates the decision-making process.
atoms.sound: Thinking for too long often complicates the decision-making process.

hint.text: Remember to look at the context of a sentence.

atoms.a: The diminishing sunset cast a beautiful light across the sky.

correct.text: Although diminishing ends in -ing, it’s used as an adjective here.
correct.sound: Although diminishing ends in i n g, it’s used as an adjective here.

atoms.a: Lucy and Zhang were exhausted from the exciting day.

correct.text: Although exciting ends in -ing, it’s used as an adjective here.
correct.sound: Although exciting ends in i n g, it’s used as an adjective here.

atoms.a: Both cycling and jogging can have a great effect on your health.
They have been mixing and creating music all night long.

correct.text: This sentence is in the present perfect continuous tense, which is formed from the verb to be and a present participle (which also ends in -ing).
correct.sound: This sentence is in the present perfect continuous tense, which is formed from the verb, to be, and a present participle, which also ends in i n g.

atoms.a: If there’s one thing he truly despises, it’s constant bickering.
